long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Foster Hamilton was an American pilot and manufacturer whose experiments helped move aviation from wood-and-fabric craft towards metal aircraft. He built gliders in Seattle before opening an aeroplane business in Vancouver, then moved to Milwaukee during the First World War to manage military propeller production. In 1927 his Metalplane venture flew an all-metal monoplane used by early airlines.

As president of United Aircraft Export Corporation, Hamilton represented American aircraft makers in Europe after overseeing construction of Burbank Airport. He also created the Malibu resort at Princess Louisa Inlet and operated a small airline serving it after the Second World War. His California estate became Hamiltair, a Lake Arrowhead community planned around private beaches, shared recreation and waterfront facilities.

Thomas Foster Hamilton, a pioneering aviator and the creator of the Hamilton Standard Company, lived from July 28, 1894 until August 12, 1969. 

Prior to World War II, Hamilton Standard (now Hamilton Sundstrand) was involved in developing propeller-driven aircraft propulsion technology since 1930. Hamilton Standard became one of the world's premier aerospace companies after the launch of Frank Caldwell's variable-pitch propeller.
